title: egress-sni-handoff-oncall-journal
content:
Context / tl;dr:
- Oncall notes capturing an odd customer report: intermittent TLS failures from private deployment (VPC-peered) to external SaaS vendor. Failures only from one AZ and only for a subset of hosts behind the egress NAT. Non-repro locally; reproducible from customer's infra and our dedicated test instance in their VPC.

What customer sees:
- Client apps intermittently fail with TLS errors when connecting to api.partner.example.com:443.
- Failures correlate with some client IPs; other client IPs in same subnet succeed.
- From our side, some connections show truncated ClientHello or server aborts with handshake_failure.

Hypothesis (quick):
1) SNI rewriting / stripping on the egress path (peering or transit) causing server to reject ClientHello (SNI mismatch -> certificate selection problem).
2) Asymmetric routing leading to middlebox reassembly/MTU issues causing ClientHello fragmentation -> server closes.
3) ECMP / SNAT inconsistency on the peering path causing return packets to hit different NAT and break 3-way handshake / TLS state.

Commands run (ordered by time) + key outputs:
1) Basic DNS / resolve checks on customer host (10.10.4.8):
   dig +short api.partner.example.com @10.0.0.2 -> 54.23.12.98
   curl -v --resolve "api.partner.example.com:443:54.23.12.98" https://api.partner.example.com/health --max-time 10
   - Success from healthy IPs, fails from affected IPs: "curl: (35) SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 54.23.12.98:443"

2) Openssl s_client with SNI and without to compare TLS handshake:
   openssl s_client -connect 54.23.12.98:443 -servername api.partner.example.com -msg -state -debug 
   -> From affected IP: TLS1.3 handshake aborted after ClientHello. Server replies: "alert handshake_failure".
   openssl s_client -connect 54.23.12.98:443 -no_tls1_3 -servername api.partner.example.com 
   -> same.

3) Tcpdump at local host (affected IP) and at egress NAT device during failing attempt:
   HOST: sudo tcpdump -nn -s0 -w /tmp/fail.pcap host 54.23.12.98 and port 443
   EGRESS (bastion): sudo tcpdump -nn -s0 -A host 10.10.4.8 and port 443
   Observed: ClientHello reaches our egress box but payload appears ~20-30 bytes shorter on egress side capture compared to host capture.
   - Host capture (first bytes of TLS):
     0000  16 03 01 00 e1 01 00 00 dd 03 03 ... <ClientHello markers> ... 00 0d 'api.partner.example.com'
   - Egress capture shows ClientHello truncated mid-extension (SNI field truncated).

4) MTU / fragmentation checks:
   ping -M do -s 1472 54.23.12.98 -> "Message too long" on affected AZ; successful on healthy AZ
   iperf between host and egress gw -> MSS clamping present on gw? found tcp_mss=1400 on SNAT rule in iptables on egress appliance.

5) SNI inspection / TLS proxy suspicion:
   On egress appliance, a transparent TLS proxy process (older version of light-proxy) was seen in process list (left over from baseline config). It advertises TLS interception in logs but only bound in one AZ.
   /var/log/light-proxy/conn.log shows: "intercept: accepted conn from 10.10.4.8:43212 -> target 54.23.12.98:443; read 512 bytes; upstream reset"

6) Reproduced on our test instance in same peered VPC and AZ: toggling MTU -> when we set host MTU to 1400 the handshake completes reliably. With MTU 1500, ClientHello truncates.

Error snippets (raw):
- curl: (35) SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL
- OpenSSL: "SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:ssl handshake failure:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1517"
- light-proxy: "error: upstream reset while writing TLS handshake"
- kernel: "IPV6: bad header, len 40" (seen on unrelated flows)

Immediate conclusions from traces:
- ClientHello is being truncated between host and egress external interface. Truncation happens after initial TLS record header (so TCP established, but record not complete when egress closes or resets).
- MTU/MSS mismatch is a strong candidate; we also have evidence of a transparent proxy that may be reading partial data then resetting upstream if it cannot parse SNI extension.
- Asymmetric/multi-path shouldn't truncate packets in-flight, but ECMP + different path MTU behavior could expose MTU difference.

Actions taken during oncall:
- Disabled transparent proxy on egress appliance in AZ-A (systemctl stop light-proxy; iptables -t nat -D PREROUTING ...). Restarted SNAT service to clear half-open flows.
- Adjusted MSS clamping to 1360 on the egress device as temporary mitigation (iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360).
- Notified partner vendor that we suspected SNI truncation and asked for server-side logs for the timestamps (they reported handshake_failure at same time windows).

Result: after disabling proxy + MSS clamp, failing host retried and handshake completed. Reproduced toggling to verify: enabling proxy again -> truncation returns.

Longer-term hypotheses and next steps:
- Root cause: legacy transparent TLS-inspection proxy leftover in image for that AZ. It attempts to read ClientHello, fails on fragmented ClientHello due to lack of proper TLS record reassembly, then resets upstream. The fragmentation is worsened by inconsistent MSS/clamping settings upstream of proxy.
- Remediation plan:
  1) Remove legacy TLS proxy from egress images (onboarding checklist + bake new AMI).
  2) Standardize MSS clamping in peering path / ensure DF bits are honored; add e2e MTU tests in infra CI.
  3) Add a small packet-capture automation: when handshake_failure spikes, automatically capture ClientHello at host and egress and stash to S3 for analysis.
  4) Add a health check that attempts a TLS1.3 handshake with large ClientHello (long SNI list) to surface fragmentation issues.

Open questions / follow-ups: 
- Why was light-proxy left enabled only in AZ-A? (likely image drift or manual config change) Need to comb config management.
- Are there other proxies (customer-managed) performing similar interception? Reach out to CS contact to ask.
- Could QUIC/HTTP3 traffic avoid the issue? Partner said they only support TLS/HTTPS on this endpoint for now.

Notes to self (if returning to this doc):
- Keep pcap sample from 2026-03-10 in /tmp/samples/pcap-20260310-sni-trunc.pcap (moved to S3 later).
- Write small python script to parse ClientHello SNI offset and detect truncation automatically (use scapy/tls-parser).
- Add test case in infra dogfood app that attempts connection with SNI length = 4k to force fragmentation.

Relevant commands to re-run quickly:
- tcpdump capture (host): sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 -s0 -w /tmp/host-clienthello.pcap host 54.23.12.98 and port 443
- tcpdump capture (egress): sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 -s0 -w /tmp/egress-clienthello.pcap host 10.10.4.8 and port 443
- check process: ps aux | grep light-proxy || true
- verify MSS on iptables: sudo iptables -t mangle -L POSTROUTING -n -v
- quick SNI handshake test: python3 -c "import ssl,socket; s=socket.create_connection(('54.23.12.98',443)); ss=ssl.wrap_socket(s,server_hostname='api.partner.example.com'); print(ss.version())"

If I had to summarize in one line for pager duty notes: "Intermittent TLS failures due to truncated ClientHello on egress path caused by legacy transparent TLS proxy + MTU/MSS mismatch; mitigated by disabling proxy and enabling MSS clamp; next step remove proxy and add MTU tests."

-- Priya
